Subject: Tenant isolation & capacity plan for MedAxis pilot

Hi Rishi,

We had a productive meeting with our engineering + security teams this morning. We're running a 3-month pilot (internal triage + clinician assist) and need guidance on whether Redwood Dedicated or a Private (customer-managed) deployment is the right starting point for MedAxis. Key constraints:

- Regulated PHI workloads (US hospitals) — strict isolation and audit/logging requirements
- Target latency: p95 < 150ms for the inference path
- Expected steady-state: ~12 QPS (text gen) with 90k tokens/day; peaks up to ~60 QPS during batch ingest windows
- Model family: 13B decoder; we'll likely use quantized variants for cost reasons
- KMS/HSM requirement for key custody; SOC2 + additional attestation needed

Can you and your team outline a couple of capacity scenarios (Dedicated reserved pool vs Private footprint), pros/cons, rough cost delta, and a suggested migration path? Procurement is copied — they will want a timeline and a procurement baseline doc.

I've attached our procurement baseline for context.

Thanks,
Elena

Subject: Tenant isolation — sizing scenarios (initial)

Elena / team — drafting two practical scenarios given the profile above. Numbers are rough order-of-magnitude estimates to inform procurement and legal. I've attached an XLS with line items.

Option 1 — Redwood Dedicated (isolated tenants on our hosted fleet)
- Footprint: 8x A100 80GB GPUs (quantized 13B) in a reserved pool with burst capacity to 12x for short windows
- Expected steady throughput: ~10–15 QPS at p95 < 150ms with continuous batching and KV caching
- Isolation: tenant-level isolation + dedicated routing, SOC2 evidence from Redwood; HSM/KMS integration (bring-your-own-key via AWS KMS or Azure KeyVault)
- Pros: faster onboarding (days), lower upfront cost, Redwood-managed ops, easy rollback to smaller variants.
- Cons: shared underlying infra (logical isolation), limits on air-gap testing.
- Rough cost delta vs Private: ~-30% TCO (hosted cheaper short-term).

Option 2 — Redwood Private (customer-managed VPC or on-prem)
- Footprint: 14–16x A100 80GB equivalent (to reach similar headroom without our shared burst pools); includes dedicated NVMe for KV cache and separate logging path
- Expected steady throughput: ~12–18 QPS at p95 ~140ms if co-located; slightly lower if on-prem depending on network egress
- Isolation: full physical separation or single-tenant VPC with customer-controlled keys/HSM
- Pros: strongest compliance posture, full control over network and audit chains, supports air-gap testing
- Cons: longer lead time (4–8 weeks for provisioning + validation), higher initial cost, ops responsibilities shift to customer or managed services add-on

Migration path suggestion:
- Phase 0 (Pilot): Start with Dedicated reserved pool (8x, commit 3–6 months) with strict routing and RBAC; enable BYOK and KV encryption; prove SLOs in region.
- Phase 1 (Validation): Parallel Private staging for air-gap testing (if required by partners) — provision small private footprint (4–6 GPUs) to validate attestation and latency.
- Phase 2 (Commit or Lift): If regulatory needs or partner attestation demand physical separation, migrate to Private footprint sized per observed telemetry; use a rolling cutover with fallback to Dedicated.

Attachments: sizing-scenarios-20280512.xlsx (cost model + rough SLO sims).

- Marissa: prepare procurement timeline and MOU draft
- Elena: confirm whether air-gap testing will be required by any hospital partners before pilot start

Karthik

Team — quick decision note so we can get procurement moving. Based on Karthik's scenarios and the customer's need for a fast pilot, my recommended path:

1) Offer a 3-month Dedicated reserved proposal: 8x A100 footprint, BYOK via customer KMS, SOC2 artifact package, per-month consumption + a capped burst allowance.
2) Include an explicit option in the MOU for a Private onboarding clause (timeline 4–8 weeks) with defined acceptance tests (latency, audit log delivery, attestation).
3) Ask Legal/Compliance to prepare a short attestation checklist and for Sales to commit to a go/no-go gate at week 8 of the pilot.

Marissa — please draft the MOU with the two-path clause and the pricing bands (monthly reserved fee + per-token overage). Rishi — I'll backstop any SLA/credit asks if the customer pushes.

Laura
